checks: New bucket starts full and spends one token
Idle expiry is at least the time to replenish the spent token
40 competing clients spend exactly five tokens while refill is frozen by a future watermark
Denied clients receive a positive retry delay
Clock regression never moves watermark backwards
TTL includes the remaining clock debt and full refill horizon
Slow refill is not erased by an arbitrary 60-second expiry
Fractional tokens retained under a rejected request
Invalid cost cannot create or change a bucket
Partial state fails rather than silently minting a full bucket
An existing key cannot silently change capacity
An idle fully-refilled bucket may disappear
Recreating an expired full bucket preserves its semantics
Script touches only its declared key
Script-cache miss is observable for safe reload
EVAL fallback executes the identical decision after cache loss
limitations: Single Redis primary, not failover/partition/replication testing
Concurrency case deliberately freezes refill with a future watermark
Docker execution is functional validation, not a throughput benchmark
